column1: # CP13 error-code taxonomy (D-022 #2, D-025 #2, owner taxonomy 2026-10-18).
# Codes describe WHAT went wrong, never which component detected it (a native
# built-in, a bytecode instruction and legacy raise the same code). The set is
# small: classes of failure; specifics go in the JSON record's `details`
# Domains: syntax.* invalid source/grammar; runtime.* language run-time
# failures (type, indexing, arithmetic, callables, bindings); io.* filesystem
# and I/O; stream.*; json.*/schema.*; process.* process execution and job
# control; host.* host integration; limit.* execution/resource limits;
# policy.*; package.*; ffi.*; user.* thrown Errors; internal.* genuine Nift
# implementation failures. Existing domains are reused where they fit.
# Catchability and severity are separate properties of each raise: renaming or
# adding a code never changes what a program can catch (all codes below that

column5: meaning
malformed expression or literal: R1-R5 (unterminated literal, brackets, empty element, missing operand)
statement form the statement grammar rejects (fn/if/while/... forms), also inside deferred bodies
undefined binding, assignment to an undefined binding, redeclaration (details.kind)
call of an unknown function or method
operand, binding or value of the wrong type
array index outside the array (negative or too large)
missing object key, member or method
wrong number of arguments
checked int64 overflow
division or modulo by zero
other arithmetic domain errors (fractional modulo, non-finite result)
argument value outside a function's domain
operation not supported on the value (string indexing, ...)
break/continue/return outside their construct
assignment to const or private state
value that cannot be rendered or projected
forged or stale handle
use of a closed or finished resource
resource used by a non-owner
prohibited resource transfer
recursion/frame budget, nesting and other explicit limits (never an ordinary exception)
memory or other resource exhausted (not an implementation defect)
non-I/O host service failure (clock, randomness, ...)
operation on a handle that was closed or reclaimed (close() itself is idempotent; D-035)
a non-handle value reached a handle position (compiler defect, W13)
a handle of another kind reached a handle position
a handle issued by another handle table (another run or isolate)
a handle that was never issued
a handle resource resolved as the wrong host type
a handle used outside its owning context (or a context nested in it)
reference counting on an uncounted handle
handle operation in an ended, ending or cancelling execution context
execution context never issued
handle kind not registered
handle kind registered twice
handle created for a null resource
Failed: known alive after forced termination, without a more specific code (D-035: nonzero exit)
Lost: a cleanup hook threw, so termination could not be confirmed
Lost: a cleanup outcome was never reported
Lost: termination could not be confirmed, without a more specific code
CleanupIncomplete: known to have ended (exited) but reaping or handle cleanup could not be completed; never 'alive'
detach inside a build (D-030); processes use process.detach_in_build
detach of a process inside a build (D-030)
detachment could not be established (ownership not transferred, or the promised lifetime cannot hold: already terminating); D-039
host-internal: a transfer that would move a resource out of a build
close() whose resource settled Failed, Lost or CleanupIncomplete synchronously; the diagnostic carries the failure's own code (D-035: exit 1)
begin_termination with a cause other than exited, deadline or cancel
close_context or shutdown called from inside a cleanup hook of the same table
